metadata.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV

problem_summary.summary: Maximize profit from at most k complete buy-then-sell transactions, never holding more than one share at a time.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: integer k and daily prices. Return the greatest total profit using no more than k transactions.

brute_force.explanation: For each day recursively consider skipping, buying when flat, or selling when holding and below the transaction limit. A completed sale increments the transaction count. This enumerates schedules and is intended only for small inputs.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every legal schedule makes exactly one of the allowed daily decisions. The recursion evaluates each such schedule, rejects unfinished holdings at the end, and returns the maximum realized profit.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(3^n) as a loose upper bound on the branching schedule search, where n is prices.length.

optimized.explanation: Maintain cash[t], the best profit while flat after at most t sales, and hold[t], the best balance while holding after beginning a transaction within limit t. For each day, derive new arrays only from the previous day's states so a buy cannot use a sale from the same day.
optimized.correctness_idea: For each transaction allowance, the only choices are to keep yesterday's state, buy today from yesterday's flat state with one fewer sale, or sell today from yesterday's holding state. Taking the maximum over these choices preserves the optimal value for every state.
optimized.time_complexity: O(nk), where n is the number of days; each day updates k transaction states.
optimized.space_complexity: O(k) auxiliary space for the current and next day state arrays.

steps.condition: No sale has happened; holding states are impossible.
steps.action: Start with zero cash profits and negative-infinity holding balances.

steps.condition: Buying from cash[0] gives balances -1 for either at-most allowance.
steps.action: Set next hold states to [-inf,-1,-1]; cash remains zero.

steps.condition: Selling yesterday's -1 holding yields 2 profit; no better buy occurs.
A second buy based on yesterday's cash[1]=2 yields balance 0.
steps.action: Update hold[2] to 0; retain first-transaction states.

steps.condition: The second holding balance 0 can be sold for total profit 4.
steps.action: Update cash states and return cash[k].

edge_cases.handling: No sale is possible, so the initialized cash profit zero is returned.
All cash states remain at zero because no sale improves profit.

edge_cases.case: k exceeds the number of possible transactions
edge_cases.handling: The at-most states permit fewer than k sales and retain the best feasible profit.
The state transitions reduce to the single-transaction buy/sell recurrence.
